::: {.manual-status}
**Resource status:** Usable beta. Adapt it to the method and check local requirements. Do not place confidential or identifiable information in a public copy.
:::

## When to use it

Use this template when the relevant reasoning needs to remain visible after the conversation or task has ended. Replace the prompts; do not leave bracketed instructions in a final record.

## Blank template

**Purpose or decision:** [What is this record for?]  
**Context:** [What has happened, and what stage is the work at?]  
**Known facts and evidence:** [Cite or link the authoritative record.]  
**Assumptions:** [What is believed but not yet verified?]  
**Constraints and local requirements:** [What limits the available choices?]  
**Options considered:** [Include realistic alternatives.]  
**Provisional recommendation:** [What should happen, and why?]  
**Owner and next action:** [Name the person and action.]  
**Evidence of done:** [What observable result will close this item?]  
**Review or escalation date:** [When will this be reconsidered?]

## Completed example

**Purpose or decision:** choose the next reversible project step.  
**Context:** the preferred activity depends on an approval that has not yet been confirmed.  
**Known facts and evidence:** the submitted request and current approved protocol are linked in the project record.  
**Assumptions:** approval may arrive this week; this is not treated as confirmed.  
**Constraints and local requirements:** no participant-facing activity may begin before written approval.  
**Options considered:** wait; prepare non-participant materials; redesign the sequence.  
**Provisional recommendation:** complete reversible preparation only.  
**Owner and next action:** researcher prepares materials and checks status on Friday.  
**Evidence of done:** materials saved in the approved project location and status recorded.  
**Review or escalation date:** Friday, or earlier if the milestone is threatened.

## What this prevents

This resource reduces decisions being lost, assumptions being mistaken for facts, and actions being marked complete without evidence.
